data.name: Just One Line
data.detailed_description:
Just One Line is a fantasy RPG gamebook-like indie game heavily focused on choices and their consequences, in which you may compete with other players in an interactive online leaderboard.
Create different adventurers by choosing their races and backgrounds and embark on a variety of epic quests: each adventurer will progress by increasing his/her renown and relations with the factions of the Kingdom thus unlocking new races and backgrounds for your next playthroughs.



Even though the core game experience is a text-adventure 2.0, anyone, of any age, who likes fantasy RPGs or books should give it a try. In fact, Just One Line has many great features appealing to a broader audience:

  • CHOICES MATTER
    A lot of games say so, but a few truly mean it. Most of the quests in Just One Line are linked together and have different story paths according to your race, background, attributes and, more importantly, choices made in previous quests.
  • ENDLESS GAME EXPERIENCE
    The video game itself is a framework upon which countless quests may be created and played. By exploiting user generated content and partnering with writers, Just One Line could potentially provide ever-growing contents!
  • YOUR ADVENTURER, YOUR STORY
    Create your adventurers as you see fit. Start by choosing a race and a background, follow up with some aesthetic customization and finally shape him/her into a valorous hero or a ruthless villain. Their morality and honor changes according to your in-game choices.
  • WILL YOU BE THE BEST?
    When you resign your adventurer you can compete with other players in the online leaderboard to be the most renowned/good/evil/rich(/whatever!) adventurer of the Kingdom!
  • HIGH REPLAY VALUE
    Each quest has choices, or even entire story paths, only available after certain conditions are met and/or depending on previous quests’ choices! Every time you play with different adventurers, the story changes.
  • ALL ABOUT IMMERSION
    We feature a unique set of locations with a fancy toon graphics and a mesmerizing OST to aid your imagination when embarking on epic quests. You will be amazed!
  • SHORT STORIES, DEEP STORIES
    We believe that wall of texts are not needed for engaging desktop players. Quest telling is rich and thrilling yet not too darn long.
  • INNOVATIVE YET CONSERVATIVE
    The concept of our game is a breath of fresh air! However, you can expect everything a role-playing gamer has come to know and love: races, classes, skills, magic, powerful weapons and armors… Oh! And dragons, zombies and pirates too!

reviews.review:
Just One Line is a fantastic concept that I really hope succeeds.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nPneay8uoKU

The basis of Just One Line is rather simple, you create an adventurer and fulfill quests that end up on a tavern job board in order to gain money, fame, glory, et cetera. It's a simple concept that the developer has turned into an extremely engaging experience with a good deal of replay value.

So you create your character and choose what you want them to specialise in. You choose either power, wit, or cunning. Basically you are good at smashing things, figuring things out or persuading people. There are different races and classes to choose from that each have their own traits, though only a few are currently implemented in the game.

Once you create your character you are suddenly in a tavern menu with a job board. After you spend some money getting basic gear, you choose from the available quests to complete during your adventure.

Each quest is a short text adventure. There is little traditional gameplay and most of it is spent reading and making choices during the quest. These choices can affect whether you pass or fail the quest, what rewards you receive and generally how people see you.

It might not sound like much, but the quests involved are all well written and offer a great amount of choices in how you complete them. There are no fail states other than dying during the quest. If you run away or refuse to do something, the quest just ends and you continue your adventure. The game is all about defining your character stories and who they are. There were times when I failed a quest but was still rewarded because I did something they didn't want me to such as literally robbing a farmer's house when he got lost. Having those choices really makes it engaging.

The quests are written very well with a few spelling errors that I noticed but nothing major. Just minor things like mispelling "the" as "teh" once or twice.

The goal of the game is to unlock more adventurers as you play by getting to certain milestones, doing certain things and the like. You can retire adventurers and make a new one to lead on a completely seperate path. The game is designed to be experienced a few times.

The game is helped tremendously by the art style. This game does a wonderful job with making a text adventure feel alive and fun to play. There are background environments and a fantastic fantasy cartoon setting that gives the game a ton of personality. More choose your own adventure games need to incorporate this because it makes the experience much more enjoyable.

There are only a handful of quests currently available for about an hour of content if you want try out a couple different characters. The developer stated they will be adding more in and also announced what I believe will be the feature that makes the game have lasting power and become popular.

The developer wants to put in the ability for players to make their own quests. This could potentially spawn an endless amount of new content for players to experience and form a great community around the game. I would advise that there be a system to help reduce griefing, as I'm sure there will be many meme related quests and the like. A list of different quest catagories would be great that players could turn on or off. That way meme or joke quests could be seperated and not forced onto players that might want something a bit more serious.

Overall, Just One Line is an absolutely fantastic idea and I genuinly cannot wait to see where this one goes. You've done good JOL Studios.


If you found this review helpful, feel free to follow my curator page to see every game I cover.
http://steamcommunity.com/groups/iampattyjack#curation
